column3: The journal is a ring of SLOTS = CHECKPOINT_ROWS + 32 slots (pi_journal_ring, PK (slot, part), WITHOUT ROWID) overwritten by upsert; a checkpoint upserts its row and parts and deletes nothing; a full ring holds the flush in memory and retries the checkpoint; a pre-ring pi_journal is replayed, checkpointed and dropped at open
column4: a DELETE bills one row written per row, so truncating 256 rows per checkpoint doubled the journal's write cost; an overwriting upsert bills one row like an insert; the legacy table is migrated by checkpoint rather than copied into slots because a home whose checkpoints failed can hold more uncovered rows than the ring has slots; the 32 spare slots, not 256, keep a cold boot's full ring scan small, and PRAGMA table_list replaces a sqlite_master scan that read 16-40 rows a boot
